title: Man killed in La Ronge standoff
subtitle: Angry worker refused to lay down his gun: [Final Edition] - ProQuest
article: --- SASKATOON - Police in Saskatchewan shot and killed a man who had barricaded himself in a hotel in La Ronge during a tense 17-hour standoff that ended early Monday morning.
According to the RCMP, 38-year-old Shawn Martinot was killed around 3:30 a.m. when he emerged from his room with a gun. He had been flushed out with tear gas, delivered by an RCMP robot.

There were reports that Martinot, an itinerant labourer, became enraged when he lost his money on VLT machines. He allegedly returned from his room with his rifle and shot up the machine, said some residents in the northern town of about 2,600.
"We have heard that rumour a number of times, but according to the staff sergeant in La Ronge, that does not appear to be the case," said RCMP spokesperson Heather Russell.
Police said the incident began around 10:30 a.m. Sunday when Martinot walked into the lounge of the hotel carrying a rifle.
Staff disarmed Martinot, but he returned to his room where he had other weapons.
The hotel and part of a neighbouring apartment building were evacuated.
The RCMP emergency response team, based in Regina, flew into La Ronge and tried to negotiate with Martinot for several hours but he refused to surrender.
After the tear gas was released, Martinot fired at the robot, disabling it. He came out of his room and walked towards police, still carrying the gun, Russell said.
He was shot and killed when he refused to put the gun down, she said.

A review of the incident will be conducted by the RCMP, which is standard procedure whenever an officer discharges a weapon. Russell could not say whether Martinot's weapon was pointed at any officers, saying that will be part of the review.
Martinot reportedly moved to La Ronge about two years ago from Flin Flon, Man.
Bill Hawke, a retiree who helps out at the La Ronge Motor Hotel where the incident happened, said Martinot had caused trouble in the past, but it always ended peacefully.
